chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Usury (riba) occurs only in what is measured by volume or weighed.'

key_terms.الرِّبَا: Usury or interest, specifically referring to the excess taken in exchange of similar commodities
key_terms.يُكَالُ: That which is measured by volume (e.g., grains, flour)
key_terms.يُوزَنُ: That which is weighed by weight (e.g., gold, silver, spices)

ai.seo_question: What types of goods are subject to the specific rules of usury (riba) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of usury (riba) is strictly confined to commodities measured by volume or weighed by weight, a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between riba al-fadl and other trade excesses. This distinction excludes goods not subject to these specific measures, thereby refining the application of the prohibition in commercial transactions. The ruling underscores the precision required in Islamic commercial law to ensure fairness and prevent exploitation in market dealings.
